What actually lives on the blockchain?

Contributions, campaign status, coffee balances, reward calculations, and redemption events. The website displays that state. Customer identity and order details stay off-chain.

Is a coffee token a share in the business?

This prototype gives you beverage credits and a fixed-term revenue-linked reward entitlement. It does not issue company equity or offer cash withdrawals. Revenue-linked benefits may still be regulated; the legal structure must be settled before a real offering.

Who verifies the café’s revenue?

In this demo, you simulate the café’s report. The contract requires the matching reward funds, but cannot prove that reported sales are complete or truthful. A live pilot needs POS reconciliation and an accountable verifier.

What does the coffee reserve guarantee?

The contract keeps payment tokens against outstanding coffee obligations. That does not guarantee the café will stay open or serve the drink, or that a real payment token retains its value. Café closure and refund terms need a separate agreement.

What happens to fractions and paused accounts?

Only whole KM can be redeemed. A leftover fraction may remain unusable when the 12-month reporting window ends; this prototype has no top-up or cash settlement. The administrator can pause successful-campaign claims and redemptions or revoke wallet approval. Failed-campaign refunds remain available.

When must revenue be reported?

This prototype accepts funded reports submitted within 12 months of campaign success. It has no grace period for late reports. A live agreement must define eligible sales periods, final settlement, and reporting deadlines.

Can I sell my tokens?

Transfers are disabled in this first version. Original reward rights stay with the contributing wallet. A marketplace, transferable rights, and associated compliance are later design decisions.

What would it take to launch?

Agree café and customer terms, confirm the legal structure, choose a settlement asset and network, integrate identity checks and the POS, audit the contracts, then run a limited testnet pilot before handling real money.
